name: BRAF mutation
summary: BRAF mutations occur in a small subset of NSCLC; BRAF V600E is a validated target for combined BRAF and MEK inhibition, whereas non-V600 mutations are mechanistically heterogeneous and lack a standard targeted option.
biology: BRAF is a RAF-family serine/threonine kinase in the MAPK cascade downstream of RAS. Class I mutations (V600) signal as RAS-independent monomers and are sensitive to current BRAF inhibitors. Class II mutations signal as RAS-independent dimers, and class III mutations are kinase-impaired and amplify signalling through RAS-dependent CRAF heterodimers; these classes are not effectively inhibited by first-generation monomer-selective BRAF inhibitors. Unlike other drivers, BRAF mutations occur in both smokers and never-smokers.
alterations: Class II: e.g. K601E, L597, G469A/V, fusions
Acquired BRAF fusions or V600E as resistance to EGFR TKIs

methods: BRAF V600E mutation-specific immunohistochemistry (VE1), research or screening use
testing.specimen: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumour tissue (biopsy, resection or cytology cell block); plasma ctDNA as a complementary or initial approach
testing.notes: Broad NGS is preferred to capture non-V600 variants and co-alterations.

predictiveRelevance: BRAF V600E predicts benefit from dabrafenib plus trametinib (and other BRAF/MEK combinations); the role of these agents in non-V600 mutations is not established. Immune checkpoint inhibitors retain activity in BRAF-mutant NSCLC, particularly in smokers, and sequencing between targeted therapy and immunotherapy is individualised.
resistance: MAPK reactivation: NRAS/KRAS mutations, MEK1/2 mutations, BRAF amplification or splice variants
cnsConsiderations: Intracranial activity of BRAF/MEK combinations has been reported, but CNS-specific data in NSCLC are limited compared with melanoma.
